review_notes:
I read the whole file. I did not open the related source files or search Mathlib, so this is a judgement from the file text alone.

The new definitions are `PushoutGluing`, `Source`, `Index`, `label`, `sourceLift`, `comparison`, `representative`, `atomLift`, `iso`, `basisIso` and `modelIso`. They are specific to this development. They are built on Mathlib's `pushout`, `IsPushout`, `IsPushout.of_iso_pushout`, `RetractArrow` and `MorphismProperty.of_retract`, and on the repo's own `OrderedAtomBasis`, `CompositionExpression` and `StrictOmegaCategory`. I found no Mathlib structure for gluing atom bases, so none of them competes with an existing Mathlib concept.

The statement `PushoutGluing.isPushout` and the one for the globe cylinders repeat the same `of_iso_pushout` proof pattern. That is duplicated proof structure, which the rubric excludes.

The two zigzag theorems, one for truncated categories and one for omega categories, are parallel theorem statements. That is also standalone theorem duplication, which the rubric excludes.

I found no justified finding. The main uncertainty is that I did not check whether the repo already has an equivalent gluing structure elsewhere.
